description: Years the product lasts before any repair
source: Engineering judgement; PVC-coated polyester membranes last ~15-20 y in service (Birdair, ETS), untreated hemp is less UV/mould-resistant outdoors but fine when sheltered
comments: Widened from 12-18 to 8-20 y because exposure is unknown (indoor/covered: 20+ y, exposed: ~5-10 y). Replace when the use case is fixed.

description: Years added to the product's life by one repair
source: Engineering judgement: a repair fixes local damage, not the ageing of the rest of the fabric
comments: Was 10 y. Set to about half of the expected lifetime (7.5 y).

parameter: share of product mass per repair
description: Mass of material added per repair, as a share of the product mass
source: Engineering judgement: patching/replacing the damaged ~10% of the membrane area
comments: Range widened to 5-15%.

description: Share of the product's end-of-life mass that goes to this route (the routes add up to 100 %): composted
source: JRC 2019 (EU post-consumer textile waste): only ~22% separately collected; of that 10% reuse, 30% recycling (mostly open-loop into rags/insulation), 50% export, 10% incineration/landfill; recycling capacity 0.7-0.85 Mt/y now, 1.5-2.0 Mt/y projected for 2030-35 (JRC134586); EEA: 73% of EU textile waste incl. mixed waste is landfilled or incinerated (2022), 26% of separately collected (15% incineration, 12% landfill split as ~56:44)
comments: Hemp is compostable in principle, but no textile composting route exists at scale; modelled as 0. NOTE: methods.md says the scaled-up variant leaves end of life unchanged, so the scaled_up values on these rows may not be read by the model.

description: Share of the product's end-of-life mass that goes to this route (the routes add up to 100 %): recycled (open loop)
source: JRC 2019 (EU post-consumer textile waste): only ~22% separately collected; of that 10% reuse, 30% recycling (mostly open-loop into rags/insulation), 50% export, 10% incineration/landfill; recycling capacity 0.7-0.85 Mt/y now, 1.5-2.0 Mt/y projected for 2030-35 (JRC134586); EEA: 73% of EU textile waste incl. mixed waste is landfilled or incinerated (2022), 26% of separately collected (15% incineration, 12% landfill split as ~56:44)
comments: Typical: ~27% of textile waste is not incinerated/landfilled (100-73%); nearly all of it is open-loop (rags, insulation), fibre-to-fibre is negligible (JRC). Scaled-up: mandatory separate collection and ~2x recycling capacity by 2030-35 (JRC) raise open-loop recycling.

description: Share of the product's end-of-life mass that goes to this route (the routes add up to 100 %): recycled (closed loop)
source: JRC 2019 (EU post-consumer textile waste): only ~22% separately collected; of that 10% reuse, 30% recycling (mostly open-loop into rags/insulation), 50% export, 10% incineration/landfill; recycling capacity 0.7-0.85 Mt/y now, 1.5-2.0 Mt/y projected for 2030-35 (JRC134586); EEA: 73% of EU textile waste incl. mixed waste is landfilled or incinerated (2022), 26% of separately collected (15% incineration, 12% landfill split as ~56:44)
comments: Typical: fibre-to-fibre recycling is still emerging in the EU (JRC). Scaled-up: a single-fibre, uncoated hemp product is ideal feedstock for fibre-to-fibre recycling with a producer take-back (scenario, RAW design intent was 80%).

description: Share of the product's end-of-life mass that goes to this route (the routes add up to 100 %): incinerated with energy recovery
source: JRC 2019 (EU post-consumer textile waste): only ~22% separately collected; of that 10% reuse, 30% recycling (mostly open-loop into rags/insulation), 50% export, 10% incineration/landfill; recycling capacity 0.7-0.85 Mt/y now, 1.5-2.0 Mt/y projected for 2030-35 (JRC134586); EEA: 73% of EU textile waste incl. mixed waste is landfilled or incinerated (2022), 26% of separately collected (15% incineration, 12% landfill split as ~56:44)
comments: Typical: 73% landfill+incineration split ~55:45 (EEA). Scaled-up: falls as recycling grows.

description: Share of the product's end-of-life mass that goes to this route (the routes add up to 100 %): landfilled
source: JRC 2019 (EU post-consumer textile waste): only ~22% separately collected; of that 10% reuse, 30% recycling (mostly open-loop into rags/insulation), 50% export, 10% incineration/landfill; recycling capacity 0.7-0.85 Mt/y now, 1.5-2.0 Mt/y projected for 2030-35 (JRC134586); EEA: 73% of EU textile waste incl. mixed waste is landfilled or incinerated (2022), 26% of separately collected (15% incineration, 12% landfill split as ~56:44)
comments: Typical: the other ~45% of the 73% (EEA). Scaled-up: 10% respects the Landfill Directive limit for 2035 (general knowledge, not re-checked online).
